subject: Islamic Studies
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y3 lesson 9 (Mushaf or printed al-Ma'idah 5:6 (translation of the meaning))
intro: Lesson 9: Purity and why we make wudu. To understand why purity matters in Islam and why wudu needs a niyyah

questions.q: Explain why someone with clean hands still makes wudu before salah.
questions.a: Wudu is not only for dirt; Allah commands it to make us pure for prayer.
questions.model: Teacher: My hands may look clean, but wudu is worship. Allah tells us to make it before salah (5:6). With my niyyah, it makes me pure.

questions.q: Name three things that must be clean for salah.
Write a short 'Why I make wudu' card on the pupil PDF: three sentences using taharah, niyyah and salah.
questions.a: For example: I make wudu to be pure for salah. My niyyah is in my heart. Allah loves those who keep pure.
questions.model: Teacher writes sentence 1: 'I make wudu because Allah tells us to be pure before salah.'

questions.q: which ayah tells us how to make wudu?
what does 'purity is half of faith' teach us?
questions.a: Purity is a big part of being a Muslim, not a small extra.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: what is the difference between clean and pure?
questions.a: Pure means ready for worship as Allah taught, with niyyah.
